headline: High: open-webui can ingest and act on content while awesome-selfhosted is a static list, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and compliance risks through shared files and external APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a static knowledge-management repo with no runtime I/O, so it cannot inject directly. open-webui can ingest local files, mounted volumes, MCP, and web content, and may treat content as prompts. The pairwise pathway exists if users copy list content or linked material into open-webui; uncertainty about exact parsing behavior keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF content from awesome-selfhosted is pasted or imported into open-webui as instructions or context, injection is possible.
IF open-webui MCP or file ingestion is enabled, attacker-controlled text can reach its prompt pipeline.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files in open-webui.
Use a read-only staging folder for imported list content.
Strip markdown links and code blocks before import.
Require human review before any MCP tool call.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted itself touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not a leak source. open-webui handles prompts, documents, files, and API keys, and can call external APIs and cloud services by default. If shared files or mounted volumes contain sensitive material, open-webui can transmit it outward; the pairwise risk is therefore medium.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the mounted volume or local files exposed to open-webui, they may be sent to external APIs.
IF open-webui is configured with third-party search or model providers, file contents can leave the host.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared folder before starting open-webui.
Disable external providers and search connectors.
Use a separate volume for non-sensitive imports.
Rotate any API keys stored in open-webui after testing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write, network, or runtime capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. open-webui can write files, use persistent sessions, and spawn subprocesses, but there is no second writer in the pair. The only plausible conflict is if the static repo is mounted read-write, which is unusual and still small in blast radius.
conditions: IF the awesome-selfhosted repository is mounted read-write into open-webui, open-webui may modify shared files.
IF multiple open-webui instances share the same mounted data volume without locking, state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Mount the repository read-only.
Keep open-webui state on a separate volume.
Avoid sharing the same data directory across instances.
Check file permissions before launch.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable storage.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a curated list, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative references. open-webui can render or act on imported content via tools, MCP, and function calling. If list entries or linked snippets are used as facts without verification, open-webui can propagate stale or incorrect recommendations; the pathway exists in default usage but is not inherently action-taking.
conditions: IF open-webui uses entries from awesome-selfhosted as factual guidance without verification, errors can cascade into downstream outputs.
IF open-webui is connected to tools that execute actions based on retrieved recommendations, the impact increases.
mitigations: Require source verification before reuse.
Show citations alongside imported recommendations.
Disable auto-action tools for imported content.
Flag stale entries for manual review.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring to retrieved facts.

E_compliance.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is an open-source directory with no data residency or retention obligations, so it is not the compliance driver. open-webui handles documents, notes, files, persistent memory, analytics, and API keys, and may send them to third-party APIs or cloud services. If regulated data is entered into open-webui, retention and residency mismatches can arise; the other agent is not cited because it does not process regulated data.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into open-webui and external providers are enabled, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF open-webui stores persistent memory for data subject content, deletion/export workflows may be incomplete.
mitigations: Do not enter regulated data into open-webui.
Disable analytics and persistent memory for sensitive sessions.
Use local-only models and connectors.
Review retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows.
